title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Everstone Studio (Where Winds Meet) describes adopting NVIDIA DLSS 5 neural rendering via its existing Streamline integration, tuning model selection and structural/tonal strength to preserve art direction. DLSS 5 adds measurable performance overhead, so it will ship as an optional, player-toggleable feature, and the studio advises budgeting for it early.

insights.claim: Everstone Studio adopted NVIDIA DLSS 5 in Where Winds Meet smoothly because it had continuously kept its NVIDIA Streamline and prior DLSS integrations up to date.
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: Prior DLSS integrations create switching costs and a fast path for each new NVIDIA feature, reinforcing ecosystem lock-in.

insights.claim: NVIDIA gives DLSS 5 developers model selection plus structural and tonal strength controls, and Everstone artists and engineers iterate on these to keep faces and colour palette from drifting off the intended look.
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: Controllability is what lets neural rendering pass art-direction review in shipped games.

insights.claim: Everstone reports DLSS 5 tones down overly bright highlights, adds ambient-light detail in shadows and recognizes material properties, with the biggest improvement in Where Winds Meet's Jiangnan region (wood and roof-tile detail).
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: Neural rendering is being used to add material detail, not just upscale, a qualitative step-up in NVIDIA's software differentiation.

insights.claim: Everstone's stated goal for DLSS 5 is harmony with existing art direction rather than greater visual impact for its own sake, checking that characters stay recognizable and materials stay distinct.
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: Studios will gate neural-rendering adoption on preserving IP identity.

insights.claim: Everstone's internal testing indicates enabling DLSS 5 introduces additional performance overhead, so Where Winds Meet will let players enable or disable it and the art team will choose the DLSS 5 model.
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: DLSS 5 is a GPU-cost feature, not a free performance win; it raises demand for GPU headroom on high-end RTX cards.
insights.quote: Our testing to date indicates that enabling DLSS 5 introduces additional performance overhead

insights.claim: Everstone advises developers to account for DLSS 5 in the rendering budget early and to reserve headroom when targeting high frame rates.
insights.speaker: Phillip Singh
insights.so_what: Signals DLSS 5 consumes meaningful frame budget, which may limit default-on adoption in high-FPS titles.
insights.quote: First, account for DLSS 5 performance requirements early in your rendering budget.
